claim.quote: We report, for the first time, the long-awaited detection of diffuse gamma rays with energies between 100 TeV and 1 PeV in the Galactic disk.

date.note: arXiv v1 date; published as Phys. Rev. Lett. 126, 141101 (2021).

name: First detection of sub-PeV diffuse gamma rays from the Galactic disk
notes: The significance is not stated in the abstract and is therefore not recorded.
The brief for this stream cited arXiv:1909.12535 for this paper; that identifier is an unrelated computer-science preprint. The Tibet ASgamma paper is arXiv:2104.05181.

official_url.quote: First Detection of sub-PeV Diffuse Gamma Rays from the Galactic Disk: Evidence for Ubiquitous Galactic Cosmic Rays beyond PeV Energies

summary.plain: The Tibet array detected a faint glow of gamma rays between 100 TeV and 1 PeV spread along the Milky Way, the first time. It matches what is expected if cosmic rays above 1 PeV are accelerated in our Galaxy and collide with interstellar gas.
summary.technical: Tibet AS + muon-detector array: diffuse gamma rays at 100 TeV - 1 PeV from the Galactic disk; all gamma rays above 398 TeV are seen away from known TeV sources and are compatible with the hadronic scenario (pi0 decay from proton-gas interactions), evidence that PeV cosmic rays are accelerated and spread in the Galactic disk.

title: First Detection of sub-PeV Diffuse Gamma Rays from the Galactic Disk: Evidence for Ubiquitous Galactic Cosmic Rays beyond PeV Energies
why_it_matters: The abstract says this is strong evidence that cosmic rays are accelerated beyond PeV energies in the Galaxy and spread over the Galactic disk.
